learning_objective: 🎯 Learn how a simple trading company from Europe slowly gained control over India and completely changed its history, economy, and society.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: In the 1600s, the British East India Company came to India just to buy spices, cotton, and silk. But when they saw that Indian kings were constantly fighting each other, they started building armies and forts to protect their trade.

The British used their military power to defeat the Nawab of Bengal at the Battle of Plassey (1757) and the Battle of Buxar (1764). These victories gave the foreign company the power to collect taxes directly from Indian citizens!

During the colonial era, India went from being one of the richest countries in the world to a poor colony. The British bought raw materials cheaply from India, made goods in English factories, and sold them back at high prices, crushing local weavers.

To move their troops and goods faster, the British introduced railways, the telegraph, and a modern postal system. While these helped India modernize, they were originally built to help the British control the country more easily.

fun_activity.title: 🌶️ The Spice Route Scavenger Hunt!
fun_activity.instructions: Go to your kitchen and find black pepper, cardamom, and cinnamon. These exact spices are what brought European ships sailing thousands of miles to India 400 years ago!

quick_recap: ⭐ The British East India Company arrived in India looking for valuable trade goods.
⭐ By taking advantage of divided Indian rulers, the traders slowly became masters of the land.
⭐ Battles like Plassey and Buxar gave the British political and financial control over rich provinces.
⭐ India's wealth was drained to Britain, making local farmers and craftsmen very poor.
⭐ The British introduced railways and telegraphs mainly to strengthen their own grip on India.
